1.explanation: The CLI’s run.js defines two functions—printErrorAndExit and printRuntimeErrorAndExit—that simply log err.friendlyMessage (or err.message) to stderr and exit. In the fatal error path, err is an instance of LighthouseError, whose constructor in lh-error.js uses i18n.createMessageInstanceIdFn (str_) to generate a template ID rather than resolving the actual localized string. Because no subsequent i18n lookup happens before printing, the CLI outputs the raw template key. To fix this, the CLI error-printing functions or the LighthouseError constructor must invoke the proper i18n formatting step (e.g. retrieving the English default messages) so that err.friendlyMessage contains the real user-friendly text instead of the template identifier.
1.bug_scenario: When you invoke the Lighthouse CLI with an invalid URL (or any URL that triggers a fatal runtime error) and pass the --view flag, the CLI falls into its error path and prints the raw ICU template identifier (“lighthouse-core/lib/lh-error.js | urlInvalid # 0”) instead of the fully formatted, localized human-friendly message (“The URL you have provided appears to be invalid.”).

2.explanation:
The core of the bug is that errors generated by LighthouseError carry an ICU template identifier in their friendlyMessage, but on the CLI’s fatal error path this identifier never gets resolved through the i18n machinery. 

– LighthouseError (in lh-error.js) is responsible for creating an i18n message instance (str_) for each error code, but if no translation step runs later, friendlyMessage remains a template key.

– printRuntimeErrorAndExit and printErrorAndExit (in lighthouse-cli/run.js) are the functions that actually print fatal errors to stderr, yet they simply pick err.friendlyMessage or err.message without invoking any i18n formatting. As a result, the raw message ID is shown instead of the localized string.

Fixing this will require invoking the i18n translation step (e.g. passing the ICU message through getFormatted or a similar function) before printing in these CLI functions.
2.bug_scenario: When the user runs the Lighthouse CLI with a URL that triggers a fatal error (e.g. an invalid URL), the CLI prints the raw ICU template identifier (“lighthouse-core/lib/lh-error.js | urlInvalid # 0”) rather than the localized, human-friendly error message.
